environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary, strict-token upstream peer, TLS via openssl s_client

findings.description: The request parser decodes the target and admits the decoded space into the normalised path used to build upout, so the upstream request line gains a fourth whitespace token with the second token exactly /exec. Over TLS the captured upstream line is byte-identical to the cleartext one: GET /exec ?cmd=id HTTP/1.1, 4 tokens, and the peer executes id. Control /api/hello.txt gives a 3-token line and no exec on both transports. Execution is sh -c on the upstream host.
findings.title: The %20-escaped space split of the upstream request line reproduces byte-identically over TLS

limitations: RCE is on the upstream host, not local
Needs the TLS listener and a proxy_pass location whose prefix can be consumed
methods: Verified the staged source is byte-identical to the tag
Compiled and ran the build against a strict-token peer
TLS control /api/hello.txt then payload /api/exec%20?cmd=id over TLS
Diffed the TLS upstream capture against the cleartext capture
